name: 1998 eye chart (A10/T50)

card.summary: A grid of eye-colour swatches from a 1990s doll-company form, rescaled online as a joking A10 to T50 status ranking and used in looksmaxxing talk about eye colour and appearance.
card.note: The ranking is a meme with no scientific basis; some uses of it carry racial overtones.

quick.overview:
The 1998 eye chart is a grid of iris-colour swatches labelled from A10 (palest blue) to T50 (darkest brown). It began as a form from a custom-doll company and was later reposted online as a tongue-in-cheek ranking of eye colours.

In looksmaxxing communities it is used as shorthand for eye-colour attractiveness and compared with metrics such as canthal tilt, and many members post it ironically.
quick.how: People use the chart to name or compare their eye colour, sometimes rating it as a tier. It is a reference image, not a technique.
quick.risks: No scientific evidence supports the tier ranking. Some posters use it sincerely in race-based arguments, which is a point of criticism.

lead: The 1998 eye chart is an internet meme based on the eye-colour section of a profile form from My Twinn, a Denver company that made custom dolls resembling real children [1]. Its swatches run from A10 (pale ice blue) to T50 (very dark brown). The chart later circulated without context and was turned into a satirical "caste" system in which light eyes sit at the top [1].

In looksmaxxing communities it is used as a lighthearted or sincere way to talk about eye colour as part of facial appearance, alongside measures such as canthal tilt [1]. The cited source notes no scientific evidence supports the hierarchy [1].

chain: Chart labels eye colours A10 to T50
Members place their own eye colour on the scale
Used as shorthand when discussing eye-area appearance
angle.text: The chart does not change appearance; it provides common vocabulary for eye colour. Followers of eye-colour ideas sometimes look at coloured contacts or other eye-area changes, which this entry does not cover.

paras: My Twinn began making dolls in 1996 and used variants of its questionnaire until around 2002; a 1998 revision expanded the colour options and gave the meme its name [1]. Sources differ on exact dates of the company's operation [1].

In the early 2000s the eye-colour grid circulated as a simple poll. The caste overlay, with A10 labelled at the top and the lowest tier labelled "Untouchable", came later, reaching 4chan's /pol/ board and iFunny, and then looksmaxxing communities [1]. Some posts are ironic; others are sincere pseudoscience, and the chart has appeared in racist posts [1].

timeline.event: My Twinn starts selling custom dolls [1].
Revision of the doll profile form expands eye colour options [1].
Approximate start of the meme's use as a caste ranking [1].
